symptom: `mxcli playwright check http://frontend.local:8180/ -p app.mpr --role R` (frontend.local an /etc/hosts name for 127.0.0.1 and the app's configured root URL, app started with `run --local --detach`) printed a rendered page (right title, text=2021) with `console-errors=2`, two `ERR    WebSocket connection to 'ws://frontend.local:8180/mxdevtools/' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 502` and `FAIL   2 console error(s)`, exit 1; the same check on http://127.0.0.1:8180/ passed with 0 console errors
cause: Not the runtime and not run --local: the runtime answers the /mxdevtools/ handshake 101 on the configured host name (curl --noproxy '*' with Host and Origin vm:18180, 11.15.0), and run --local puts nothing between browser and runtime. The 502 is the environment's HTTPS proxy. Chromium on Linux takes its proxy from the environment and, for a WebSocket, prefers the HTTPS proxy even for ws:// (RFC 6455 4.1.3). With only https_proxy set, every http:// load of the app went direct, while ws://frontend.local:8180/mxdevtools/ went to the proxy because no_proxy listed localhost and 127.0.0.1 but not the app's own name; the Claude Code agent proxy cannot reach this machine's loopback and answered `502 upstream request failed` (curl -p -x $HTTPS_PROXY: 200 Connection Established, then 502)
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/browser_proxy.go (directRouteEnv), called where mxcli starts a browser at the app: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck.go (ProbePages), screenshot_login.go (LoginAndSaveStorage, SignOut), screenshot.go (CaptureScreenshot)
fix: the browser mxcli starts gets every host among its URLs that resolves only to this machine (loopback, or an address of one of its interfaces) appended to no_proxy and NO_PROXY, when the environment configures a proxy; the proxy settings themselves are untouched, so a remote --hub URL still uses it. No console error is ignored: the channel connects, and a genuine console error still fails the page
insight: The report called /mxdevtools/ mxcli's own channel and offered two fixes (ignore it in the verdict, or make run --local serve it on the configured host); both assumed the server answered 502 on that host. One curl straight at the runtime with the configured Host (101) and one through the proxy (502 'upstream request failed') settled who answers, and three standalone Playwright runs of the same page settled the route: env as is -> 502; the name appended to no_proxy -> 0 errors, 2 frames received; https_proxy unset -> 0 errors. The tell was the shape of the failure: the page loads, only the WebSocket fails, and only on a name not in no_proxy. Ignoring the channel in the classifier would have passed the page while the channel stayed broken in that browser, and an app's own ws:// to its host would still have failed the check. Repro without /etc/hosts edits: a Claude Code container maps `vm` and `runsc` to 127.0.0.1 and neither is in no_proxy, so `ApplicationRootUrl http://vm:<port>/` reproduces the report byte for byte. A unit test needs no host name either: an httptest page on the machine's own non-loopback address (Chromium bypasses only loopback by itself) plus a fake CONNECT proxy that answers the tunnelled request 502 reproduces the message verbatim. Scope: env proxies are what Chromium reads on Linux; macOS and Windows Chromium read the OS proxy settings, which this does not touch
test: cmd/mxcli/docker/browser_proxy_test.go (TestDirectRouteEnv_*: loopback name and interface address added; remote, split, unresolvable, already-listed, no-proxy and unparsable left alone; both no_proxy spellings; IPv6 bracketed); cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_proxy_test.go (TestProbeReachesALocalAppsDevChannelDirectly: the real probe against a fake dev-mode page behind a refusing proxy, with an in-test control that reproduces the 502; skips without Node/Playwright).
